summary: Three narrow, well-scoped ERP PM gap closures: PMS timesheet-to-invoice generation (new pms-invoice-service.ts reusing the existing erp_sales_invoices/erp_sales_invoice_items tables, gated by a real DB transaction via withTenantContext so the invoice insert, line-item inserts, and time-entry invoiceItemId backfill are atomic -- the anti-double-billing mechanism is sound), cross-project resource-conflict detection (detectResourceConflicts/getResourceConflicts, correctly distinct from the existing single-project getWorkload()), and a verified no-op for the Gantt/critical-path UI gap (confirmed via direct code read that PROJEXA's ScheduleGanttClient.tsx already ships this, merged 2026-07-09 -- not just trusted self-report). Verified by direct inspection, not the PROGRESS.md narrative: the billable-rate resolver correctly returns null (not a silent 0) so invoicing can never zero-bill an unconfigured rate; the migration's ADD CONSTRAINT-without-IF-NOT-EXISTS and the invoice-numbering max()+1 pattern both match pre-existing, established conventions elsewhere in this repo (0086_wave108, erp-invoicing-service.ts) rather than being new bugs; all new routes are correctly org-scoped and auth-gated (requireAuth for the money-moving invoice route, requireAuthOrApiKey+requirePmsEnabled for the compliance-tracker-facing conflict routes, no gate on the v1/projexa routes matching that directory's own established convention); unit tests cover the real edge cases (overlap boundaries, at-capacity-exactly-not-flagged, missing-rate-throws, org-default-fallback). No .github/workflows/** changes in this diff. Tier2 is correctly assigned (touches schema.ts and a *.sql migration) and this diff should still be held for human sign-off per that policy, but on the merits it is ready to merge.
issues: Minor, not blocking: /api/pms/invoices/generate calls requireErpEnabled() but not requirePmsEnabled(), so an org with PMS explicitly disabled but ERP enabled could still generate an invoice from pre-existing pms_time_entries rows -- worth a follow-up gate for defense in depth, not a real exploit path today.

Minor, not blocking: dailyCapacityHours query params that fail Number() parsing (e.g. '?dailyCapacityHours=abc') become NaN and silently suppress all conflict detection instead of erroring -- pre-existing pattern in this codebase (same shape as the sibling workload route), not introduced by this diff, but still worth tightening.
